business.about: CreditAccess Grameen Limited is registered as a non-deposit accepting NBFC - Microfinance Institution with the RBI. It is engaged in providing microfinance services to women who are enrolled as members and organized as Joint Liability Groups. It also uses its distribution channel to provide certain other financial products and services to the members. [1]
business.in_their_words: Now the credit cost since we are publishing within the guided range and being driven by the pricing policy, this will be range bound.

results.read: Revenue +26% YoY; PAT +298% — profits outran sales.

calls: Margins compressing: 18% latest vs 25% average of prior years
Weak cash conversion: 5-yr operating cash flow is -3.15× reported profit
Free cash flow negative in 4 of the last 5 years

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: We raised our profitability guidance for FY27, ROA of 5.2% to 5.8% versus 4% to 4.8% earlier and ROE of 21% to 24% versus 16% to 20% earlier.

items.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
items.quote: So in the second half, even if it slightly inches up, maybe even if we go to 5% run rate, still for the full year, we should be within 4% and today like I said in my previous response the NIMs what we have they are well enough to cover 4% kind of a credit cost and still deliver the ROA what we are aiming for.

items.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
items.quote: So on a risk-adjusted basis, the NIM is more than, I mean, it's closer to 11% to more than 11% and we would want to retain a risk adjusted NIM of 10% so that it allows us to achieve our targeted ROA of 4.5% to 5% on a steady-state basis.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio improved to 28.2% and PPOP grew 39.6% YoY and 11.2% QoQ to INR 970 Crore in Q2 FY27.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: We expect a NIM of 14.4% to 14.7% as against 12.8% to 13.2% guided earlier, driven by healthy asset quality, strong control over borrowing costs and a higher capital position even after factoring the 50-bps rate reduction applicable from October onwards.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Our annualized H1 FY27 credit cost of 3.43% includes normative credit cost of 2.98% and 0.45% of macroprudential buffer, which is well within our guided range.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Over the past 6-plus years, involving 4 years of stress events, that is 2 years of COVID and 2 years of MFI credit cycle, the company's net worth increased from INR 2,734 Crore in FY20 to INR 8,347 Crore in Q1 FY27, compounding at 20% CAGR, of which 86% increase came just through internal accruals.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: The average PAR 15 accretion rate for Q1 FY27 stood at ~15 bps per month, whereas the credit cost for the quarter stood at INR 212 Crore or 0.72% on a non-annualized basis, comfortably within our guided range.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: As a result, our Q1 FY27 PAT grew 720% YoY to INR 493 Crore, resulting in an ROA of 5.9% and ROE of 24.4%.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Our ability to demonstrate quick recovery helped us report strong improvement in our return ratios in Q4 FY26 and further in Q1 FY27, thus helping us to improve our trailing 12-month ROA to 4% and ROE to 16%, both aligned with our guided cross-cycle profitability metrics.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: We continue to see the scale-up of our retail finance book, which now constitutes 20.6% of the AUM, up 250 bps sequentially from 18.1% in Q4 FY26.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: And importantly, employee attrition continued to moderate meaningfully, standing at 20.6% as of Q1 FY27 against 25.8% in Q1 FY26.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: For FY27, we are guiding an AUM growth of 20.0-25.0%, NIM of 12.8-13.2%, cost to income of 33.0-35.0%, credit cost of 3.0-4.0%, ROA of 4.0-4.8%, and an ROE of 16.0-20.0%.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Disbursement in Q4 grew 28.4% YoY, and 44.1% QoQ to INR 8,313 Crore, while the full year disbursements came in at INR 24,859 Crore, up to 24.1%.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: The AUM grew 14.0% YoY and 11.4% QoQ, in line with the annual growth guidance, despite 7.6% write-offs made in FY26.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: FY17 to FY26, we have compounded AUM at 28.6% per annum, disbursement at 24.7% and PAT at 29.7%.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: While our PPOP was in line with the budget, our credit cost ended at 6.74% as against the guidance of 5.5% to 6.0%.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: The additional 0.64% credit cost due to increase in ECL rates resulted in marginal miss on the lower end of our ROA and ROE guidance of 2.9% and 11.8%, respectively.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Net interest income grew 13.4% YoY to INR 977 Crore with portfolio yield of 21.0% versus 20.7% in Q2 FY26.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Our FY27 credit cost guidance of 4% to 4.5% reflects a new PAR 15 accretion rate of 30-35 bps per month.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: The disbursements for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 5,767 Crore, increasing by 13.4% YoY with the exit month December crossing INR 2,200 Crore mark.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: We wrote off INR 259 Crore worth of loans in Q3, which includes INR 181 Crore of accelerated write-offs pertaining to 180 DPD non-paying accounts, leading to additional credit cost of INR 59 Crore in Q3 FY26.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: The credit cost for Q3 FY26 stood at INR 343 Crore, which includes INR 59 Crore due to accelerated write-off and INR 37 Crore due to additional impact due to increase in ECL rates.

items.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
items.quote: So maybe for next year, we should see the NIMs anywhere between maybe 14% to 14.5%, in that range for some time because borrowing cost incrementally, we do see dropping by 10 bps every quarter for at least next 2 to 3 quarters, then it should settle down.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Since the PAR accretion rate is 40-45 bps as against 25-30 bps expected, every month of delay in PAR accretion improvement is resulting in an additional credit cost of 15-20 bps.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Our average cost of borrowings continues its downward trajectory, having declined 11 bps to 9.6% at the end of Q2 FY26.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Our foreign borrowings stood healthy at 23.7%, progressing toward our medium-term target of achieving 25–30% foreign borrowings by FY’28.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: Hence, the overall credit cost may range in 4-4.5% in FY’27, including the one-time ECL rate revision of 70-80 bps.

items.speaker: Nilesh Dalvi
items.quote: We are envisaging that the next year credit cost would be in the range of 4% to 4.5%.

items.speaker: Ganesh Narayanan
items.quote: So that means we are talking about 20% in H2 to reach the guidance that we have given, and we are confident of doing that.
